digest.component_or_area: plan-review severity grading, review_kernel impact model
propositions: The undecomposed axis fires on 0.107% of plan-v3 verified findings (11/10,250) and 0.153% of plan-v4 (18/11,773), two orders of magnitude below other severity axes, but its floor at 0.85 is the sole hard override in 25 of 29 fires.

The stated justification for low fire rate—a G5 deterministic suppressor that filters false flat-plan findings on tickets with children—is factually inert: the suppressor never fired (0 vetoes across 2,000 reviews) and is inapplicable to 90%+ of reviewed tickets which are childless.

The axis gates the 0.85 hard-override floor on all non-none grades uniformly, so low-grade fires (16 of 29) floor to the same 0.85 impact as high-grade fires, causing a low-grade alone to block at least one finding.

The inverse-population search (findings whose text matches the undecomposed regex but scored axis=none) yields 33 plan-v3 and 17 plan-v4 matches, but sampled inspection confirms these are false positives (code decomposition and module seams) rather than missed flat-plan defects.

The calibration defect parallels prior fixes to ac_unverifiable and divergent_implementation: a hard-override axis flooring on its weakest grade without distinction, requiring gating the floor on grade severity.
